The paper sets out an idealized three-stage sequence of interaction types, which it calls a "first and rough sketch" (§1). Stage 1 is coordination in *collections* (pairwise, "aggregative" interactions of co-located individuals). Stage 2 is cooperation in *conexuses* (a connected web of binary interactions whose benefits can still be counted per member). Stage 3 is collaboration in *communities*: heterogeneous multi-way interactions around a shared goal, in which generatively entrenched "core" interactions give organizational closure. Table 1 puts the transition to a new level of individuality between stages 2 and 3 only. The paper asserts, rather than argues, that this describes evolutionary transitions non-circularly and that individuality is a special case of collectivity. Its one argued conclusion is hedged: community-level inheritance "seem[s] likely to evolve in tandem" with community-level individuality (§3). | Proposed — read in full 2026-09-26 ([NOTE-173](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-173.md)); a short programmatic sketch, and the authors call it one. A depth-3, width-200 ReLU MLP trained on 1,000 MNIST images (the Omnigrok recipe, with weights and biases scaled ×8, MSE loss, AdamW, WD = 0) for 10⁷ steps goes through three phases read off the accuracy curves. In pre-grokking (to ~10⁵ steps) training accuracy saturates while test accuracy stays low. In grokking (~10⁵–10⁶) test accuracy rises to ~0.85. In "anti-grokking" (~10⁶–10⁷) it falls to ~0.45–0.5 while training accuracy stays near 1. The average HTSR power-law exponent α of the two hidden weight matrices goes 4.0 → 2.9 → 1.1 at the phase ends (Table 1). In the collapse phase, correlation traps (outlier eigenvalues of the elementwise-shuffled weight matrix) appear. The paper's own weight-decay control shows FC2's α below 2, and traps in both layers, *without* a collapse (Fig. 6, Table 2). That undercuts its headline claim that α < 2 "invariably" heralds collapse. | Proposed — read in full 2026-09-30 ([NOTE-317](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-317.md)); worth knowing as the report of a late generalisation collapse after grokking at WD = 0, but it is one architecture on one 1k-sample MNIST subset, with the seed count unstated, and its central diagnostic (α < 2 ⇒ collapse) is contradicted by its own WD = 0.01 control. What would settle it: several seeds and architectures, with α and traps reported for runs that reach α < 2 without collapsing, and a comparison against the ℓ² norm under the Omnigrok LU account, which the paper does not cite. |
| [LIT-370](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-370.md) v2 | New Evidence of the Two-Phase Learning Dynamics of Neural Networks | Zhou et al. (2025), arXiv:2505.13900. VGG-16 and ResNet-20 on CIFAR-10 (SGD with momentum, lr 0.1, 160 epochs) are compared across pairs of training times. Before an early "inflection point" (~2,500 iterations for VGG-16, ~100–500 for ResNet-20), a tiny parameter perturbation under identical SGD noise sends the run to a different basin by the end: loss barrier up to ~2, test disagreement ~0.15–0.5. After it, the same perturbation leaves the runs linearly connected. Also after it, the empirical NTK keeps changing step to step but stays within a bounded cosine distance of any later reference kernel (the "cone effect", e.g. S ≈ 0.05–0.1 for VGG-16 vs ≈ 0.15–0.2 from initialisation). Switching to linearised training later gives better test accuracy (VGG-16 0.13 → 0.82 as the switch moves from ≤200 to 5,000 iterations). | Proposed — read in full 2026-09-30 ([NOTE-318](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-318.md)); a compact, readable demonstration that an early, short chaotic phase gives way to a confined, stable one in both basin and kernel terms, but it rests on two architectures on one dataset, one run each with no error bars. The chaos half largely re-measures Frankle et al.'s (2020) spawning / linear-mode-connectivity result with a parameter perturbation in place of fresh SGD noise, and the claimed role of the cone in generalisation is asserted. What would settle it: seeds and error bars, the batch size, a stated perturbation norm, other domains, and a quantitative test of confinement (e.g. an angular radius that stops growing) rather than a 3-D picture. |
